meta.description: Genuine Coelho. The line is dialogue in Part Two of The Alchemist (1988), spoken by the alchemist — not a sourceless motivational aphorism.
meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'There is only one thing that makes a dream impossible to achieve: the fear of failure'?
meta.ogDescription: It really is Paulo Coelho — a line from The Alchemist, Part Two, in Alan R. Clarke's 1993 English translation of the 1988 Portuguese original.

answer.label: Written by
answer.sourceLine: This one is real. It is a line of dialogue in Part Two of Coelho’s novel The Alchemist — first published in Portuguese as O Alquimista in 1988, and rendered into English by Alan R. Clarke for HarperSanFrancisco in 1993. Wikiquote’s sourced section carries it under The Alchemist and attributes it to the alchemist character.

source.excerpt: There is only one thing that makes a dream impossible to achieve: the fear of failure.
trail: Coelho published the novel in Portuguese as O Alquimista in 1988, in a small Brazilian print run from Rocco — the publication history is set out on Wikipedia’s article on the novel ↗.

The English text everyone quotes comes from Alan R. Clarke’s translation: Open Library’s record for the HarperSanFrancisco first English edition ↗ gives 1993, 1st ed., 177 pages, “translated by Alan R. Clarke.”
Wikiquote’s sourced section ↗ carries the sentence under The Alchemist (1988) at p. 141 and attributes it to the alchemist — not to Coelho narrating.
Two independent study guides put it in the same place: LiteraryDevices ↗ lists it as a Part II line spoken by the alchemist, and Shmoop ↗ quotes it verbatim with the citation 2.600.
source.excerptNote: The novel is in copyright, so only the sentence itself is reproduced here rather than the surrounding passage. In context it is spoken by the alchemist during the desert episode in which Santiago is challenged to turn himself into the wind. Shmoop ↗ cites the line as 2.600 — Part 2 — and Wikiquote ↗ gives p. 141, while one page-numbered index ↗ gives p. 146 in the HarperOne 25th-anniversary edition. Pagination differs between editions; the Part Two placement is consistent.

source.rightsNote: The Alchemist was first published in 1988 and its English translation in 1993, so both the Portuguese original and Clarke’s English rendering are firmly within copyright — nowhere near the pre-1931 line for US public domain. The sentence is quoted here briefly for identification and criticism, with the source named; it is not free to reproduce at length.

author.name: Paulo Coelho
author.heading: Who was Paulo Coelho?
author.metaLine: b. 24 August 1947, Rio de Janeiro · Brazilian novelist and lyricist
author.bio: Paulo Coelho was born in Rio de Janeiro on 24 August 1947 and worked as a songwriter before turning to fiction. The Alchemist, his fable about a shepherd boy named Santiago who crosses the desert in search of treasure, began life as a small Brazilian print run in 1988 and became one of the most translated books by a living author. Wikipedia reports his work has sold some 320 million copies and been translated into 83 languages — which is also why his name has become a magnet for feel-good lines he never wrote.

misattribution.heading: What still gets it wrong
misattribution.intro: The attribution to Coelho is correct — which is rarer than it sounds for a name this heavily quoted. What goes wrong is everything around it: who is speaking, whose English it is, and whether anyone can point to a page.

items.who: Paulo Coelho, quoted as if in his own voice
items.why: It is not an authorial maxim. Wikiquote’s sourced section ↗ attributes the line to the alchemist character, and LiteraryDevices ↗ places it in Part II with the alchemist as speaker. Coelho wrote it; a character says it.

The English everyone shares is Clarke’s. Open Library’s record for the 1993 first English edition ↗ lists it as translated by Alan R. Clarke, and Portuguese collections give the original as the shorter “Só uma coisa torna um sonho impossível: o medo de fracassar” (Citador ↗). The words “to achieve” are the translator’s.

Pages such as Quotefancy ↗ print the sentence over a photograph with nothing but “— Paulo Coelho”: no book, no page, no translator. That is the same presentation used for lines he never wrote, which is why a correct attribution here still deserves a citation.

items.who: Paulo Coelho, for lines that are not his
items.why: Coelho attracts fabrications. Wikiquote’s Misattributed section ↗ records “God is where you let Him in” as originating with the Kotzker Rebbe, and notes that “May love be your guide in every moment of your life” has not been found in available editions of his work.

misattribution.truthLine: The sentence is genuine Coelho: Wikiquote ↗ lists it in its sourced section under The Alchemist (1988), spoken by the alchemist, and study guides independently locate it in Part Two of the English translation.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: The sentence does not arrive as a motivational poster. It lands in the tensest stretch of the novel: Santiago and the alchemist are seized crossing warring desert territory, and the alchemist calmly announces that the boy will turn himself into the wind — a thing Santiago has no idea how to do. Wikipedia’s plot summary ↗ describes the episode as Santiago being forced to demonstrate his oneness with the Soul of the World by becoming a dust storm.

That is the setting for the line, and it changes its meaning. It is not advice about ambition in the abstract; it is said to someone who has just been handed an impossible task and three days to do it. Strip the scene away — as almost every quote-graphic does — and it flattens into the generic uplift that sourceless aggregator pages ↗ serve up with no book, page or translator attached.
detailsBody: Portuguese quotation collections record the original as “Só uma coisa torna um sonho impossível: o medo de fracassar” — see Citador ↗. The Portuguese is terser: it says simply that one thing makes a dream impossible. The familiar English “impossible to achieve” is Alan R. Clarke’s expansion, and it is his phrasing, not Coelho’s Portuguese, that circulates on the internet.
context.pull: It is a line spoken to a boy who has three days to become the wind.

sourcesVerified.claim: Wikiquote's sourced section lists "There is only one thing that makes a dream impossible to achieve: the fear of failure" under The Alchemist (1988), at p. 141, attributed to the alchemist character; its Misattributed section records "God is where you let Him in" as originating with the Kotzker Rebbe and notes "May love be your guide in every moment of your life" has not been found in available editions.

Open Library's edition record for ISBN 0062502174 gives The Alchemist, HarperSanFrancisco, San Francisco, 1993, 1st ed., 177 pages, by-statement "Paulo Coelho ; translated by Alan R. Clarke", a translation of the Portuguese O Alquimista (1988).

The Alchemist was first published in Portuguese as O Alquimista in 1988 in Brazil by Rocco; the plot includes Santiago being forced to demonstrate his oneness with the Soul of the World by turning himself into a dust storm.
Shmoop's Alchemist "Fear" quotes page reproduces the sentence verbatim with the internal citation 2.600, i.e. Part 2 of the novel.
LiteraryDevices lists the sentence as Quote #7 from The Alchemist, identifies the speaker as the alchemist, and places it in Part II.
Citador records the Portuguese original from O Alquimista as "Só uma coisa torna um sonho impossível: o medo de fracassar."
Quotefancy prints the quotation credited only to "Paulo Coelho", with no book title, page number, translator or other source.

A page-numbered index of Alchemist quotations gives the sentence at p. 146 of the HarperOne 25th Anniversary Edition translated by Alan R. Clarke, while warning that page numbers vary across editions.
Goodreads lists the quotation as by Paulo Coelho, from The Alchemist.

Paulo Coelho was born 24 August 1947 in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil; he is a Brazilian lyricist and novelist; The Alchemist was published in 1988 with an initial print run of 900 copies; his books have sold some 320 million copies and been translated into 83 languages.
A Portuguese quotation index attributes "Só uma coisa torna um sonho impossível: o medo de fracassar" to O Alquimista, citing the Pergaminho 2001 edition (ISBN 9727110797).
